scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You take a photo in a dark room, hold still for a few seconds, and it comes out surprisingly bright. How?

scenes.name: problem
scenes.text: A phone camera sensor is tiny, so it catches very little light. One long exposure would just come out blurry from your shaking hands.

scenes.name: burst
scenes.text: So night mode quickly takes many short photos in a row, sometimes a dozen or more, over a few seconds.

scenes.name: align
scenes.text: Software lines up all the frames, correcting for your hand movement, so the details sit exactly on top of each other.

scenes.name: merge
scenes.text: Then it blends them. Real details repeat in every frame, but random noise doesn't, so averaging cleans the image.

scenes.name: tone
scenes.text: Finally, it brightens the shadows, keeps lights from blowing out, and fixes colours, often with help from AI.

scenes.name: tip
scenes.text: That's why it asks you to hold still. Lean on something, and the result gets even sharper.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Burst, align, merge, brighten. Seeing in the dark. Follow for more on how things really work.
